이사야-64-1.title: 이사야 64장 1절 역사문법적 주해
이사야-64-1.exegesis: 19. thine ... never-- rather, "We are Thine from of old; Thou barest not rule over them" [Barnes]. Lowth translates, "We for long have been as those over whom Thou hast not ruled, who are not called by Thy name"; "for long" thus stands in contrast to "but a little while" ( Is 63:18 ). But the analogy of Is 63:18 makes it likely that the first clause in this verse refers to the Jews, and the second to their foes, as English Version and Barnes translate it. The Jews' foes are aliens who have unjustly intruded into the Lord's heritage.

이사야-64-2.title: 이사야 64장 2절 역사문법적 주해
이사야-64-2.exegesis: CHAPTER 64 Is 64:1-12 . Transition from Complaint to Prayer. 1. rend ... heavens-- bursting forth to execute vengeance, suddenly descending on Thy people's foe ( Psa 18:9 ; 144:5 ; Ha 3:5 , 6 ). flow down-- ( Jud 5:5 ; Mi 1:4 ).

이사야-64-4.title: 이사야 64장 4절 역사문법적 주해
이사야-64-4.exegesis: 3. When-- Supply from Is 64:2 , "As when." terrible things-- ( Psa 65:5 ). we looked not for-- far exceeding the expectation of any of our nation; unparalleled before ( Ex 34:10 ; Psa 68:8 ). camest down-- on Mount Sinai. mountains flowed-- Repeated from Is 64:1 ; they pray God to do the very same things for Israel now as in former ages. Gesenius, instead of "flowed" here, and "flow" in Is 64:1 , translates from a different Hebrew root, "quake ... quaked"; but "fire" melts and causes to flow, rather than to quake ( Is 64:2 ).

이사야-64-5.title: 이사야 64장 5절 역사문법적 주해
이사야-64-5.exegesis: 4. perceived by the ear-- Paul ( 1Co 2:9 ) has for this, "nor have entered into the heart of man"; the virtual sense, sanctioned by his inspired authority; men might hear with the outward ear, but they could only by the Spirit "perceive" with the "heart" the spiritual significancy of God's acts, both those in relation to Israel, primarily referred to here, and those relating to the Gospel secondarily, which Paul refers to. O God ... what he ... prepared-- rather, "nor hath eye seen a god beside thee who doeth such things." They refer to God's past marvellous acts in behalf of Israel as a plea for His now interposing for His people; but the Spirit, as Paul by inspiration shows, contemplated further God's revelation in the Gospel, which abounds in marvellous paradoxes never before heard of by carnal ear, not to be understood by mere human sagacity, and when foretold by the prophets not fully perceived or credited; and even after the manifestation of Christ not to be understood save through the inward teaching of the Holy Ghost. These are partly past and present, and partly future; therefore Paul substitutes "prepared" for "doeth," though his context shows he includes all three. For "waiteth" he has "love Him"; godly waiting on Him must flow from love, and not mere fear.

이사야-64-6.title: 이사야 64장 6절 역사문법적 주해
이사야-64-6.exegesis: 5. meetest-- that is, Thou makest peace, or enterest into covenant with him (see on Is 47:3 ). rejoiceth and worketh-- that is, who with joyful willingness worketh [Gesenius] ( Ac 10:35 ; Joh 7:17 ). those-- Thou meetest "those," in apposition to "him" who represents a class whose characteristics "those that," &c., more fully describes. remember thee in thy ways-- ( Is 26:8 ). sinned-- literally, "tripped," carrying on the figure in "ways." in those is continuance-- a plea to deprecate the continuance of God's wrath; it is not in Thy wrath that there is continuance ( Is 54:7 , 8 ; Psa 30:5 ; 103:9 ), but in Thy ways ("those"), namely, of covenant mercy to Thy people ( Mi 7:18-20 ; Mal 3:6); on the strength of the everlasting continuance of His covenant they infer by faith, "we shall be saved." God "remembered" for them His covenant ( Psa 106:45 ), though they often "remembered not" Him ( Psa 78:42 ). Castellio translates, "we have sinned for long in them ('thy ways'), and could we then be saved?" But they hardly would use such a plea when their very object was to be saved.

이사야-64-7.title: 이사야 64장 7절 역사문법적 주해
이사야-64-7.exegesis: 6. unclean thing-- legally unclean, as a leper. True of Israel, everywhere now cut off by unbelief and by God's judgments from the congregation of the saints. righteousness-- plural, "uncleanness" extended to every particular act of theirs, even to their prayers and praises. True of the best doings of the unregenerate ( Php 3:6-8 ; Tit 1:15 ; He 11:6 ). filthy rags-- literally, a "menstruous rag" ( Le 15:33 ; 20:18 ; La 1:17 ). fade ... leaf-- ( Psa 90:5 , 6 ).

이사야-64-8.exegesis: 7. stirreth-- rouseth himself from spiritual drowsiness. take hold-- ( Is 27:5 ).

이사야-64-9.title: 이사야 64장 9절 역사문법적 주해
이사야-64-9.exegesis: 8. father-- ( Is 63:16 ). clay ... potter-- ( Is 29:16 ; 45:9 ). Unable to mould themselves aright, they beg the sovereign will of God to mould them unto salvation, even as He made them at the first, and is their "Father."

이사야-64-10.exegesis: 9. ( Psa 74:1 , 2). we are ... thy people-- ( Jr 14:9 , 21 ).
이사야-64-10.theologicalNote: 9. ( Psa 74:1 , 2). we are ... thy people-- ( Jr 14:9 , 21 ).

이사야-64-11.title: 이사야 64장 11절 역사문법적 주해
이사야-64-11.exegesis: 10. holy cities-- No city but Jerusalem is called "the holy city" ( Is 48:2 ; 52:1 ); the plural, therefore, refers to the upper and the lower parts of the same city Jerusalem [Vitringa]; or all Judea was holy to God, so its cities were deemed "holy" [Maurer]. But the parallelism favors Vitringa. Zion and Jerusalem (the one city) answering to "holy cities."

이사야-64-12.title: 이사야 64장 12절 역사문법적 주해
이사야-64-12.exegesis: 11. house-- the temple. beautiful-- includes the idea of glorious ( Mr 13:1 ; Ac 3:2 ). burned-- ( Psa 74:7 ; La 2:7 ; 2Ch 36:19 ). Its destruction under Nebuchadnezzar prefigured that under Titus. pleasant things-- Hebrew, "objects of desire"; our homes, our city, and all its dear associations.
